html:
Milestone 1 validation — October 9, 2026

Implemented version: 0.1.0. The original roadmap remains a planning document; this record describes work actually exercised in this checkout.

Check Evidence
Unreal plugin compilation ForgeMCPDevEditor / Win64 / Development, UE 5.6.1: Result: Succeeded; original plugin DLL linked
Automated server tests 14 passed, including a real MCP subprocess handshake and all five tool schemas/results
Python lint Ruff check passed for server, add-on, scripts, and tests
Live MCP tool calls All five tools returned successful structured results through SDK stdio client
Unreal inspection Separate editor process, null renderer; actual project ForgeMCPDev, UE 5.6.1, editor world /Temp/Untitled_1.Untitled_1
Actor inspection 144 loaded actors; requested sample limit 10 correctly reported truncated: true
Blender inspection Separate factory-startup background Blender 5.2.2 LTS process; scene Scene, 3 objects, 24 FPS
Live rejection probes Each adapter rejected bad tokens, unsupported protocol versions, and execute_python; split TCP request framing handled
Codex registration CLI codex mcp get majestic_forge reports enabled stdio server with the project environment
Blender local installation Add-on file installed in Blender 5.2 user scripts directory; Blender's native add-on discovery found exactly one majestic_forge module; persistent enablement not changed

The validation Blender process explicitly pumped the bridge timer callback on its main thread because background mode has no interactive timer loop. This proves bpy inspection and network integration in a real Blender process, not interactive timer behavior in the user's open Blender window. The Unreal probe loaded the plugin and inspected the real editor world without saving assets.

Runtime evidence is stored under Saved/MajesticForgeValidation and excluded from source control. Session credentials are never included in the live report. Isolated probe processes are stopped after validation; the user's existing editor and Blender processes are preserved.

Codex client acceptance completed — October 9, 2026

All five mcp__majestic_forge__* tools were available and successfully invoked directly from the user's Codex IDE conversation, using explicit session IDs for the application calls. Each returned ok: true, structured MCP content, and isError: false.

Tool Confirmed result from the user's open application sessions
forge_status Version 0.1.0, stdio, two responding read-only adapters
forge_list_sessions Connected Unreal session unreal-40584 and Blender session blender-43952
unreal_project_info ForgeMCPDev, UE 5.6.1, world /Temp/Untitled_1.Untitled_1, PIE inactive
unreal_list_actors 144 loaded actors; sample of 10 with truncated: true; actor IDs, labels, classes, and paths returned
blender_scene_info Blender 5.2.2 LTS, unsaved Scene, zero objects, frames 1–250, current frame 1, effective 24 FPS

These calls used the user's normal application processes, not the earlier isolated probes. The live Blender bridge responded through its interactive application timer. No restart or add-on activation was necessary in this acceptance turn: both bridges were already connected. No scene, asset, or preference changes were made.

The first milestone's five-tool client acceptance criterion is satisfied. Persistence of Blender add-on enablement across a future restart has not been tested. No UI screenshot/click-through test was performed. Blueprint creation, scene modification, export/import, packaging, and public publication are future milestones.

Blender sidebar update — add-on 0.1.1

Added a 3D Viewport sidebar tab named Majestic Forge, a Forge MCP Connection panel, bridge start/stop operators, status/endpoint/session display, last authenticated request timing, and an auto-start add-on preference. Tokens are not displayed. Scene data is not changed by the panel or connection controls. Auto-start is applied when the add-on is enabled, with persistence controlled by Blender's normal preferences.

Installed the updated module in the Blender 5.2 user add-ons directory, preserving a backup of the previous installed source. A separate factory-startup Blender 5.2.2 process verified native panel registration, start/stop operators, disable/re-enable, auto-start true/false behavior, and unchanged scene object/frame/FPS state. The installed add-on verification printed FORGE_INSTALLED_UI_PREFERENCES_AND_LIFECYCLE_PASS. Python lint and all 14 server regression tests passed.

These are native Blender API checks, not a screenshot or visual inspection of the sidebar. An already-running Blender process must reload the updated add-on to show the tab; copying the source file does not replace its in-memory module. No open scene was closed or saved and no user preference file was rewritten by this update.

Unreal panel and installable plugin — version 0.1.1

Implemented a native Slate dockable Majestic Forge panel and a Window > Majestic Forge menu entry. The panel exposes bridge status, local address/session ID, last authenticated request timing, start/stop controls, and a per-project auto-start checkbox. No authentication token is displayed. The checkbox applies at the next project launch and writes only its Majestic Forge editor setting when the user changes it. Scene and asset data is not modified by the connection controls.

Epic's AutomationTool BuildPlugin compiled and linked the Win64 UnrealEditor target, then reported BUILD SUCCESSFUL with exit code 0. The package's module BuildId matches the installed engine's 43139311. The local ZIP is Artifacts/MajesticForge-0.1.1-UE5.6.1-Win64.zip and includes the native plugin source and the compiled editor binary. No public publication or distribution license was chosen. Python regression tests still report 14 passed and Ruff checks passed.

The installer was exercised twice against a separate UE 5.6 test project: initial installation enabled Majestic Forge while preserving its description and an unrelated disabled plugin; repeat installation created a backup of the previous plugin and project descriptor. It checks for a running editor before replacing target binaries.

The packaged plugin was loaded in a separate installed test project's real editor process. Authenticated health returned version 0.1.1, and project inspection returned ForgeInstallCheck. The isolated editor was then stopped. The installer's running-editor guard was also verified against the original open ForgeMCPDev project.

Native compilation, packaging, installation, and live loading are verified. No screenshot or menu click-through verification has been performed. Existing editors must be closed before their loaded plugin binary is replaced.

After the original editor was closed, scripts/Install-ForgeUnreal.ps1 installed the compiled 0.1.1 package into ForgeMCPDev itself and enabled its project plugin entry. The previous plugin was backed up under Saved/MajesticForgeInstallBackups, and the project descriptor was backed up beside the original. ForgeMCPDev was reopened using its existing Unreal 5.6.1 installation. The panel entry is Window > Majestic Forge. Direct Codex forge_list_sessions subsequently confirmed the reopened project session unreal-6528 responding with adapter version 0.1.1. The user's reopened Blender session also reported 0.1.1. Both updated bridges are live.

Security update — version 0.1.2

Both adapters now protect their credential directories and registration files before advertising a session. Windows runtime checks confirmed protected DACLs containing only OWNER RIGHTS and SYSTEM and actual Forge TCP listeners at 127.0.0.1. The existing user session directories/files were also restricted immediately. A protection failure prevents new bridge startup. Unreal tokens now use 256-bit BCryptGenRandom; Blender retains Python's cryptographic secrets generator. Tokens remain absent from panels, results, diagnostic object representations, and logs.

Added bounded JSON nesting, object argument validation, safer malformed registration handling, linked/out-of-root registration rejection, generic bridge error reporting, and explicit response bounds. The native allowlists still expose inspection only.

Check October 9, 2026 evidence
Python regression and MCP subprocess tests 22 passed
Python lint Ruff passed for server, tests, scripts, and add-on
Dependency advisory audit pip-audit 2.10.1, 38 pinned packages, no known vulnerabilities
Native editor target UE 5.6.1 Win64 Development: Result: Succeeded; original native C++ compiled and DLL linked
Installed Unreal package probe Separate ForgeSecurityCheck project loaded adapter 0.1.2
Live rejection probes, both adapters Bad token, arbitrary execution command, unsupported protocol, invalid arguments, deeply nested JSON, and oversized input rejected; both answered health afterward
Live MCP subprocess probes All five tools returned successful structured results with server 0.1.2; later environment-forwarding verification showed those calls targeted the original 0.1.1 adapters. Separate 0.1.2 rejection/health probes did target the isolated adapters.
Native permissions and listener check Both fresh token files have protected owner/SYSTEM DACLs; Forge TCP listeners are loopback only
Installed Blender verification Factory-startup Blender 5.2.2 LTS printed FORGE_INSTALLED_UI_PREFERENCES_AND_LIFECYCLE_PASS; scene state unchanged
Running-editor installer guard Refused to replace the original open ForgeMCPDev plugin

AutomationTool's initial build and subsequent UBT child launches stalled in this environment. The MSVC compile/link and UBT metadata steps completed with redirected diagnostic output, and the final UnrealEditor target check reported success. Compiling without shared PCH also exposed a missing JSON print-policy include, which was fixed explicitly. The 0.1.2 package was assembled from the compiled native output, source, descriptor, and matching engine module metadata, then installed and live-tested. Its local ZIP is Artifacts/MajesticForge-0.1.2-UE5.6.1-Win64.zip; SHA-256 is BFBE3A63B25D306897EE95886B4E2EA3C0980219C9607E15B1785EEE8A285DD7.

Evidence is under Saved/SecurityAudit and excluded from Git. The audit result is a dated known-advisory check, not a guarantee against every defect. See Security.md [not indexed] for threat boundaries.

The user's original Unreal session unreal-6528 and Blender session blender-44324 were preserved and still reported adapter 0.1.1 during this update. Blender 0.1.2 is installed on disk; the Unreal 0.1.2 package is ready for the installer. Save and close the target Unreal editor, run scripts/Install-ForgeUnreal.ps1, then reopen it. Save work and restart Blender, and restart the Codex extension to load server 0.1.2. No interactive panel screenshot/click-through validation was performed in this update.
